title: Rethinking Time Encoding via Learnable Transformation Functions
authors: Chen, X.; Tang, Y.; Xu, J.; Zhang, J.; Zhang, S.; Peng, S.; Zheng, X.; Xiong, Y.
tldr: Proposes Learnable Transformation-based Generalized Time Encoding (LeTE), a novel time encoding method using deep function learning to parameterize learnable non-linear transformations, enabling modeling of diverse and complex time patterns including periodic, non-periodic, and mixed patterns.
problem_and_motivation: Existing time encoding methods (hand-crafted and functional) rely on pre-defined inductive biases, particularly trigonometric functions for periodicity, making them less effective in handling diverse real-world time patterns. They struggle to capture non-periodic patterns and require additional dimensions for complex temporal dynamics. Real-world data often exhibits complex interplay of mixed patterns (periodic and non-periodic) that current methods cannot effectively model.
approach: Proposed LeTE (Learnable Transformation-based Generalized Time Encoding) using deep function learning techniques to parameterize non-linear transformations.
Developed three variations: Fourier-based LeTE (for periodic patterns), Spline-based LeTE (for non-periodic patterns), and Combined LeTE (integrating both).
Proved that LeTE is a generalized version of previous methods (Time2Vec, FTR) and encompasses them as specific cases.
Demonstrated LeTE satisfies time rescaling invariance property required for time representations.
Applied extensive experiments across diverse domains: event-based image classification, time series forecasting, dynamic graph representation learning, and real-world applications.
findings: LeTE achieves superior results with fewer dimensions than previous time encodings due to learnable transformations capturing complexity.
Fourier-based LeTE effectively models periodic patterns while Spline-based LeTE better captures non-periodic patterns.
Combined LeTE leverages strengths of both approaches for enhanced pattern capture.
LeTE is provably a generalized version of previous methods (Time2Vec, FTR, absolute position encoding).
LeTE satisfies time rescaling invariance property, ensuring compatibility across different time scales.
Experiments demonstrate LeTE's versatility and effectiveness across multiple domains and tasks.

key_equations.explanation: Core LeTE formula where ω_i and φ_i are learnable parameters, and ϕ_i are learnable functions parameterized by Fourier series or B-splines.

key_equations.equation: ϕ_i(x) = a_0 + Σ_{k=1}^K (a_k cos(kx) + b_k sin(kx))
key_equations.explanation: Fourier-based LeTE parameterization using learnable Fourier series expansion for periodic patterns.
Spline-based LeTE parameterization using B-spline basis functions for flexible non-periodic pattern modeling.

key_equations.equation: TE(t)[i] = sin(ω_i t + φ_i) or ω_i t + φ_i
key_equations.explanation: Previous functional time encoding (Time2Vec) that LeTE generalizes as a special case.

definitions.definition: A time encoding method using deep function learning to parameterize learnable non-linear transformations, enabling modeling of diverse and complex time patterns.
Feature mappings from 1-dimensional input time to high-dimensional time embedding using pre-defined non-linear transformations like trigonometric functions.
A functional time encoding method that uses learnable linear transformations combined with fixed sine functions for time representation.
Mathematical representation of a function as a combination of sine and cosine functions with learnable coefficients and frequencies.
Piecewise polynomial basis functions used for flexible function approximation in Spline-based LeTE.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper makes significant contributions to time encoding methods by proposing LeTE, a generalized framework that addresses limitations of previous approaches. The key innovations include: (1) using learnable non-linear transformations instead of fixed functions, (2) proving that LeTE encompasses previous methods as special cases, (3) demonstrating time rescaling invariance property, and (4) achieving superior performance with fewer dimensions. The mathematical framework provides theoretical foundation while extensive experiments validate practical effectiveness across multiple domains.
directly_justifies: LeTE achieves superior results with fewer dimensions than previous time encodings.
